profile.facility_type_note: Part of Digital Realty's Silicon Valley (Santa Clara/San Jose area) data center campus, one of the company's largest US clusters. Two facilities in this group carry independent historic significance: 360 Spear Street and 365 Main Street in San Francisco are separate, well known carrier hotel buildings; 365 Main Street was the site of a widely covered July 2007 power outage that took down major web services including Craigslist and other sites hosted there, later becoming a Digital Realty/Digital Realty-heritage asset. SJC10 is documented at 1100 Space Park Drive per Digital Realty's own site.

reading.body:
Digital Realty's SJC29 facility in Santa Clara occupies 39,500 to 40,000 square feet with 2N cooling redundancy, but publishes no megawatt power capacity figure, making actual compute density impossible to verify.

The facility holds four certifications: PCI DSS for payment card environments, ISO 27001 for information security management, ISO 9001 for quality processes, and LEED for energy and environmental design. These qualify the building to host specific workload categories but do not identify actual tenants or confirm whether the space includes AI-grade infrastructure such as high-density power delivery or liquid cooling. Floor area alone cannot reveal compute capacity. A typical colocation facility runs 150 to 200 watts per square foot, which would suggest 6 to 8 megawatts across this building, but that is an assumption applied to a floor-area figure, not a published specification.

Among California's 103 mapped facilities in this dataset, only five have published any megawatt figure at all, totaling 170 MW. SJC29 contributes zero to that total. Silicon Valley's land and power constraints are widely documented in public reporting, but no grid or power detail for this address appears in the operator's public specification. For readers tracking AI scaling against power availability, the absence of a power figure is itself the fact. Compute demand cannot be estimated from physical footprint, and this facility's role in grid constraint analysis remains indeterminate.
